law: REGISTRATION of E-Q22 — the axis-calibration x ternary-quantization factorial (ORCH-R24 lane T15-b). The question map's 8-axis vectors exist in TWO representations (ordinal score levels 0-4, the E-Q21 incumbent; noul calibrated mass p in [0,1], this lane's new arm) and TWO precisions (continuous; median-centered TERNARY codes in {-1,0,+1}). This is qthe's namesake made literal — Quilt-Ternary Hyper-Embeddings has never yet QUANTIZED an embedding to the ternary alphabet — and it experimentally answers jev-lattice's published finding (their typesafe deep-dive: score criteria levels are ordered but NOT numerically calibrated) on OUR cosine geometry. Committed BEFORE ANY EMBED CALL.
provenance_of_the_question: Operator dispatch r24 ('go a lot deeper with your JEV-as-embedder idea… this could be big… many more novel ways') + the jev-lattice recon (R24-RECON-LATTICE, synergy ideas #1 and #6, open questions #1 and #4: are noul-probability axes better embedding axes than score levels, and do ternary-quantized 8-axis vectors retain retrieval). The three-way convergence: qthe's identity (ternary alphabet in the project name, no ternary-quantization experiment yet), the lattice's calibration confound (levels ordered but uncalibrated), and the typesafe API's own division (noul = calibrated mass).

design_frozen.corpus: THE SAME sealed E-Q21 corpus (situations/embedding_r23/corpus.json, 20 records, 4 families x 5, sha frozen in the e_q21 chain). No re-draw, no edits — F1 pins the sha.
design_frozen.arms: S = score-continuous (incumbent: E-Q21 sealed rows typesafe_embed_rows_r23.jsonl, jev-latest, /4 normalized — NO new calls); N = noul-continuous (NEW: the same 8 axis CONCEPTS as noul questions 'Does this record concern X?' with true/false criteria; the answer's noul p in [0,1] IS the axis value; 20 records + 3 stability repeats N1/P4/A5 = 23 batched calls, jev-latest, one call per record with all 8 questions); TS = score-ternary (derived from S in code); TN = noul-ternary (derived from N in code).
design_frozen.ternarization: Per axis a over the 20 CORPUS vectors of the parent arm: m_a = median, MAD_a = median absolute deviation. tern(x) = +1 if x > m_a + 0.5*MAD_a; -1 if x < m_a - 0.5*MAD_a; else 0. The m_a/MAD_a table is derived from corpus vectors ONLY (never from query-time data), frozen in the results file, and recomputable by the checker (F6).
design_frozen.eval: Identical protocol to E-Q21: each record's own vector queries Cloudflare Vectorize (index qthe-jev-embed, 32-dim cosine, AM1 zero-pad carries over; ternary vectors upserted as -1/0/+1 floats under arm-prefixed ids eq22S:/eq22N:/eq22TS:/eq22TN:), top-1 non-self WITHIN-ARM family accuracy over LIVE REST queries. Baselines: majority 0.25, permutation null (1000 draws), BOW 0.80 (all sealed from E-Q21).
design_frozen.ternary_code_stats: Per ternary arm: per-axis mass on {-1,0,+1}, code entropy in bits/axis, count of distinct codes, code collisions (records sharing a code), and the storage receipt: 8 ternary axes = 16 bits vs 8 float32 = 256 bits = 16x representational compression (honest note: Vectorize internally stores float32 — the compression claim is about the embedder's OUTPUT representation, portable to any ternary-native store).
design_frozen.stability_band: F5 for the noul arm uses 0.10 (calibrated mass; the r12 finding — noul repeats stable to ~2 decimals — licenses a TIGHTER band than the score arm's 0.25).

floors.F1: corpus.json sha equal to the sha sealed in the e_q21 chain rules row
floors.F2: all 23 noul rows complete: 8 noul answers each, p in [0,1], http 200
floors.F3: all four arms' vectors recomputable from sealed rows by an independent recompute
floors.F4: all four arms upserted AND live-queried through the Vectorize REST round-trip
floors.F6: the ternarization table (m_a, MAD_a per arm) recomputable from the arm's corpus vectors; ternary vectors equal tern(parent) on recompute

hypotheses.H1_calibration: N top-1 accuracy > S top-1 accuracy (0.70) — calibrated mass beats ordinal levels (C17 LIVES iff strict >; equality = calibration-neutral receipt; N < S = C17 DIES with the ordinal-geometry-survives finding)
hypotheses.H2_ternary_survival: TS >= S - 0.15 AND TN >= N - 0.15 (the ternary alphabet keeps all but <= 3 records of the parent's retrieval)
hypotheses.H3_ternary_floor: both ternary arms > majority (0.25) AND > permutation null (0.2122) — the 16-bit code still carries the family signal
hypotheses.H4_interaction: ternarization does not INVERT the calibration effect: (TN - TS) has the same sign as (N - S) or shrinks it toward 0
hypotheses.C16: ternary quantization of question-map embeddings retains retrieval signal at 16x representational compression — LIVES iff H2 AND H3
hypotheses.C17: noul-calibrated axes outperform ordinal score axes for retrieval — per H1's three-way rule

predictions.P1: N lands in [0.65, 0.90] — same axis concepts, calibration should recover the two jev calibration-cost records of E-Q21
predictions.P2: TS lands in [0.60, 0.75] — family structure is coarse enough to survive 3 levels (<= 2 records lost vs S)
predictions.P4: ternary code entropy < 2.0 bits/axis (mass concentrates on 0 and one sign per axis — records are typical on most axes, distinctive on few)
predictions.P5: noul stability 24/24 within 0.10, tighter than the score arm's 0.25 band would have been
predictions.P6: the Q family (loosest cluster, the crossover records) pays the largest ternarization cost

falsifier: ANY of F1-F6 breached; a checkpoint written before its floor passes; the accuracy comparison computed on anything but the sealed family labels; the ternarization table computed from anything but the arm's own 20 corpus vectors; a query that skips the LIVE round-trip.
budget: 23 typesafe calls (~$0.01 ceiling) + Vectorize free tier + $0.00 moth. Round-level budget registered in the r24 registration commit.
